runs.name: Presidio Property Trust, Inc.
runs.box: OUT AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **$0.859** (close 2026-10-12, Yahoo chart endpoint through `tools/sources.py`, aggregator, flagged; below Nasdaq's $1.00 minimum bid; the 9.375% Series D preferred $6.15 against a $25.00 preference). Shares **2,258,185** Series A common: 1,434,432 on the cover of the 10-Q for 2026-06-30 (acc 0001437749-26-027591, the count including 117,493 unvested shares per the 424B3 of 2026-09-02, acc 0001493152-26-041167; the 1-for-10 reverse split of 2025-05-19 already in it) plus 823,753 issued in the Series D exchange offer that expired 2026-10-02 (149,773 of 973,736 preferred tendered, about 15.4%; Schedule TO-I/A 0001493152-26-045707, 8-K 0001493152-26-045704); 823,963 preferred remain; cap **$1.94M** (common only). Sovereign **5.60%** (USD; US Treasury daily par yield curve, 30-year, 2026-10-09). Filings read: 10-K FY2025 (filed 2026-03-27, acc 0001437749-26-010114), the 10-Q above, DEF 14A of 2026-04-21 (0001493152-26-018340), 8-Ks of 2025-05-16, 2025-10-14, 2026-01-23 (default notice, 0001493152-26-003424), 2026-01-28 (preferred dividend suspended, 0001493152-26-004044), 2026-02-18 (receiver, 0001493152-26-007357), 2026-09-02 and 2026-10-05, the exchange prospectus, the 10-Ks for FY2017, FY2019, FY2021 and FY2023. One figure cross-checked: FY2025 operating cash $417,870 filed, equal to the tagged figure; a second check found FY2023 operating cash $1,489,839 as filed against $1,448,573 in the next 10-K's XBRL, unexplained, the as-filed figure used. `tools/run.py` produced no arithmetic line ("UNRESEARCHED", no overlapping facts); every figure taken by hand from the filed statements. Ten balance sheets (2016 to 2026-06-30) read in Step 0: real estate $240.5M to $95.0M, mortgages 62% to 75% of total assets, accumulated deficit -$106.6M to -$173.3M, equity before minority interests $13.9M under the $20.6M preferred preference. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7, as the overnight brief directs (office and industrial occupancy and rent over the span; competitors' pricing; properties lost to lenders and impairments; the model-home part and its concentration; debt, maturities and the preferred; the uses of money). Competitors: the 10-K names no rival, only classes of rival; the analyst took two SEC-filing office REITs with Denver office, Franklin Street Properties and City Office REIT, and said they are not named rivals. **Q1 IN**: office and industrial rent plus model homes leased back to builders, economics foreseeable in kind, the filer stating the direction (about $4.0M of revenue lost with Dakota Center and Shea Center II, Item 7). **Q2 OUT**: the deciding part, office and industrial at 54% to 65% of segment NOI in every year 2021 to 2025 by the filer's own risk factor, is a castle shown open on the evidence: the filer writes that competitors with "substantially greater financial resources" set the rents and that space offered cheaper elsewhere forces cuts and concessions (Item 1 and 1A); office occupancy 88.1% (2017) to 82.1% (2025) while the portfolio was halved (1,463,390 to 758,175 square feet); Shea Center II (bought 2015 for about $25M to $26M) foreclosed 2026-07-01 on a $12.0M credit bid and Dakota Center (bought 2011 for $9.6M) sold 2026-01-14 for $5.125M with the lender taking the proceeds; impairments in 2020, 2021 and 2023 to 2026; head-office cost $5.7M against $10.7M of segment NOI (2025); the field's returns over the full cycle ordinary or worse (FSP leased 89.7% to 68.9% and losses of $45M to $53M a year 2023 to 2025; CIO losses 2023 and 2024, then taken private and delisted). The model-home part (about 69% leased to one homebuilder) carried, not deciding. Q3 to Q12 not reached; no research pass. After the stop, recorded not weighed: operating cash $2.4M (2021) to $0.4M (2025), negative in 2024; Core FFO, the proxy's pay measure, negative 2023 to 2025; material weaknesses in internal control and auditor changes in 2024 and 2025; two non-recourse loans unpaid at maturity; $22.6M of debt with recourse to the company; the preferred dividend suspended from January 2026 and accruing; integrity facts recorded, not judged: the company's sponsored SPAC left Conduit Pharmaceuticals stock carried at $18.3M (2023) and $3,900 (2025) against a cost basis of about $7.5M, headquarters space leased to a company owned by the chief executive and his wife, consulting fees to a director's father-in-law, buybacks at an average $4.79 and a $6.80 tender in 2025 justified by "embedded value" in the years the buildings were impaired and surrendered, the 2026 exchange issuing 57% more common. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: window 2021 to 2025, the literal one, said to be generous since it includes buildings sold or lost; owner cash (operating cash less building additions, tenant improvements and leasing costs; the REIT pays almost no company tax) average -$2.21M after interest, $2.75M all-equity; growth by specific (b) -9.0% a year carried as the bottom, no growth the top; net debt $61.0M after the Shea foreclosure; range **-$16.23 to -$5.29 a common share** all-equity against $0.859; floor tested first, no case earns it; fair price beneath the stop **below zero on both bases** (-$17.54 all-equity; equity-only below zero); not armed (box not OUT at Q7). The analyst confessed one CONVENTION of this run: the preferred's preference and arrears and the minority interest deducted in a figure shown beside, -$29.34 to -$18.41. Contamination declared by the analyst: the session's opening git status and commit subjects (MSM, the AYI and ARCB folder names) and a memory line on queue counts, none concerning SQFT; one listing of `Test Runs/` filtered for sqft, presidio and netreit before the copy, to avoid overwriting, returned nothing. Commits 1901c2c1, ab3fb3e7, f274c463, 61564300. Citations: the analyst's check PASS (36 ids, 0 problems); the dispatcher's script (`dispatcher_check.py`) found every id in the ledger and no E-id; its 16 unmatched hits are filing quotations sharing a paragraph with ids and one parse artifact, 0 slips. Position note filled at the fold (not held). check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) Q7 deducts net debt only and has no rule for a senior perpetual cumulative preferred or for minority interests; here the preference is about ten times the common's market value; (2) the business-of-parts threshold asks for five-year operating profit, which a REIT does not report by segment (segment NOI is before corporate cost, here more than half of it); (3) the window has no specific for a business selling itself down, so the average includes assets no longer owned; (4) Q1's routing speaks of fast-moving technology and does not say where a slow shift in customer demand (office under remote work) belongs; (5) `tools/run.py` produced nothing for a filer that tags tenant improvements rather than capital expenditure. The analyst could not read CIO's leased rates before 2024 or the 2025-06-05 auditor-change 8-K (item list only), or check ATM sales after 2026-08-13 beyond the filings read.
runs.narr: Q2 OUT: a small office and industrial REIT with a model-home leaseback side whose deciding part, office and industrial, is a castle shown open on the evidence: the filer's own words that better-funded competitors set the rents, occupancy 88.1% to 82.1% while the portfolio was halved, two buildings surrendered to lenders in 2026 at about half their cost, head-office cost more than half of segment NOI, a field (FSP, CIO) of ordinary returns or worse; Q1 IN. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: range -$16.23 to -$5.29 a common share all-equity against $0.859, no case earns the floor; fair price below zero on both bases, not armed. After the stop, integrity facts recorded, not judged: the sponsored SPAC's stock written from $18.3M to $3,900, headquarters space leased to the chief executive's company, buybacks and a $6.80 tender above every case of the range; the preferred dividend suspended and the common below Nasdaq's minimum bid.
